I hate it when people use their phones in movies because it's distracting and ruins the experience for everyone else. I couldn't help but have a strong reaction to this. They usually display these rules before the movie starts or have signs in the lobby. So, the woman should have been aware of this rule. On the other hand, she claims it was an emergency. Emergencies do happen, and sometimes people need to use their phones. But in this case, she didn't seem to be in a hurry or showing signs of distress beyond just texting. Also, she had a young child with her, which might have been a reason to be more understanding, but she still chose to text during the movie. I threw popcorn at her, which is a form of physical action. While it wasn't harmful, it was definitely disruptive and could be seen as aggressive. She reacted by yelling at me, and I responded by telling her to put her phone away. This escalated the situation, leading to her leaving the theater and coming back to yell at me again. I think about whether I should have handled the situation differently. Maybe instead of throwing popcorn, I could have approached her more calmly and asked her to put her phone away. But she was sitting in front of me in big recliner seats, which would have required me to stand up and walk over to her, which might have been awkward or intrusive. Also, she left the theater after a few minutes, so my action did lead to her leaving, which was good for me because I could enjoy the movie without her phone distractions. But she came back during the credits, which shows that she was still upset about the situation. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe I could have signaled to her in a less confrontational way, like making eye contact or gesturing for her to put her phone away. But I was already frustrated, and my reaction was immediate. Another thing to consider is the impact on others. The woman had a young child with her, and by storming out, she might have caused disruption for her child as well. But I was focused on enjoying the movie, and her actions were affecting my experience. I also think about the concept of "theater etiquette." Most people go to the movies to escape and enjoy the film without distractions. Breaking the rules by using a phone can be seen as disrespectful to others. So, in that sense, I was trying to uphold the rules and maintain the experience for everyone. However, resorting to throwing popcorn can be seen as overreacting. It's a form of self-help that might not be the best approach. It could have led to more conflict or even physical harm if she had reacted differently. In the end, I think the situation was a bit of a lose-lose. I wanted to enjoy the movie, and she wanted to use her phone, which I found disruptive. On the other hand, she was breaking the rules by using her phone in the theater, which was disruptive to my experience. Maybe the best approach would have been to politely ask her to put her phone away or inform the theater staff if she continued to be disruptive. Throwing popcorn, while it got her to stop, wasn't the most mature or effective way to handle the situation. In conclusion, while I understand why I reacted the way I did, there was a better way to address the issue without escalating it. So, in that sense, I was partly in the wrong for overreacting.
